name: SikaBond-105 ContactFix
paste:
SIKABOND®-105 CONTACTFIX: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: SikaBond®-105 ContactFix, November 2025, Version 03.01 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/f/sikabond_-105_contactfix.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide SikaBond®-105 ContactFix where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (November 2025, Version 03.01).
1.2 Product description. SikaBond®-105 ContactFix is a premium contact adhesive that has been formulated to meet varied needs for lamination and fabrication. SikaBond®-105 ContactFix is fast drying and forms a strong bond that is heat and water resistant.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. SikaBond®-105 ContactFix has a very broad adhesion range and forms a strong and lasting bond. Suitable substrates are timber, rubber sheets, plastic laminates, fabric, cloth backed and polyester backed vinyl, MDF, particleboard, concrete, glass and metal sheets. In the production of transport vehicles SikaBond®-105 ContactFix is suitable for room temperature contact bonding of different covering materials e.g. PUR foams, textiles, adjoining steps, wheel arches, seat brackets and side walls, especially for covering materials with high spring-back forces, cover trims and edging profiles. SikaBond®-105 ContactFix is also suitable for auto upholstery and furniture upholstery. Test with actual substrates and conditions to ensure adhesion and material compatibility.
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.5.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. SikaBond®-105 ContactFix
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: HIGH STRENGTH PREMIUM CONTACT ADHESIVE
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals, certificates and standards stated by the manufacturer. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (November 2025, Version 03.01) has no approvals, certificates or standards section.
2.3 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - One-component adhesive
    - Short flash-off time
    - High initial strength
    - Easy to apply
    - Resistant to ageging
    - High heat resistance
    - Broad adhesion range
    - Fast dry time
2.4 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: One-component polychloroprene
    - Colour: Light Amber
    - Density: 0.81 kg/l
2.5 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Consistency: 350 mPa.s
    - Solid content by mass: ~17%
    - Tack free time: ~ 5-8 minutes
2.6 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 500mL, 1L, 4L Can; 20L Pail
    - Shelf life: 12 months from date of production
2.7 Storage conditions. The product must be stored in original, unopened and undamaged sealed packaging in dry conditions and out of direct sunlight at temperatures between +5°C and +25°C. Always refer to packaging. Refer to the current Safety Data Sheet for information on safe handling and storage

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (November 2025, Version 03.01) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate preparation. The adhesion surfaces must be sound, clean, dry and free of all contaminants such as dirt, oil, grease, poorly bonded coatings, loose and friable materials.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (November 2025, Version 03.01) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Consumption: 6 - 8m²/ Litre
4.3 Application method / tools.
    - The adhesive is generally applied with a suitable roll-coater, tooth-comb, brush or spray gun. Apply to both surfaces evenly, wait until touch dry, normally 5-8 minutes depending on drying conditions, bring the surfaces together, applying even pressure along the entire bonding surface.
    - Care must be taken to avoid the formation of adhesive pools on the bonding surfaces. Entrapped solvent causes weak bond.For application on open weave or porous materials, spray apply the adhesive to avoid adhesive bleed through the substrate. Once the container is opened, the material must be consumed in a short time.
4.4 Cleaning of equipment. Uncured SikaBond®-105 ContactFix may be removed from tools and equipment with Sika® Remover-208, Sika® Colma Cleaner or other suitable solvent. Once cured, hardened material can only be removed mechanically. For cleaning skin use Sika® Cleaner-350H.
4.5 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Do not use in temperatures below +10° C, condensed water may form on adhesive and prevent bonding.
    - For best results apply at ambient, material and adhesive temperatures of +20° C.
    - Do not apply excessive adhesive, allow adhesive to pool or apply the two substraes together too early. This will cause entrapped solvents which will cause a weak bond or bond failure.
    - Coverage rate, flash off time, open time and press time are dependant on the type of materials to be bonded and ambient temperature and humidity.
    - Adhesion tests on specific substrates must be performed prior to use.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Temperature resistance. up to 90°C
5.3 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.5):
    - Do not use in temperatures below +10° C, condensed water may form on adhesive and prevent bonding.
    - For best results apply at ambient, material and adhesive temperatures of +20° C.
    - Coverage rate, flash off time, open time and press time are dependant on the type of materials to be bonded and ambient temperature and humidity.
5.4 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.5 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: SikaBond®-105 ContactFix, November 2025, Version 03.01, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/f/sikabond_-105_contactfix.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS SikaBond®-105 ContactFix, version 02/02/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/w/sds-sikabond-105contactfix.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
